papers.title: Designing Attention-Driven Play: A Multi-Genre Suite of BCI Games
papers.reason: The paper appears to involve attention-based BCI interaction, which is relevant to attention measurement but seems focused on game design rather than executive-function modelling or clinical assessment.

papers.title: [Neurocognitive characteristics in children with sluggish cognitive tempo].
papers.reason: The study combines clinical child groups, working-memory and attention testing, TOVA, and EEG spectral measures to characterize SCT and ADHD-related cognitive impairment.

papers.title: Neural Differences Between Prosocial and Self-Serving Lies: A Review of Evidence from Cognitive Neuroscience
papers.reason: The review discusses prefrontal and anterior cingulate mechanisms of cognitive control in deception, but executive function is only one component of a broader social-neuroscience topic.

papers.title: The Association Between Socioeconomic Status and Academic Achievement Mediated by Psychological Factors
papers.reason: The proposed theoretical model includes central executive functioning and working-memory depletion, but the paper is mainly about educational inequality rather than computational modelling of executive function.

papers.title: Spatial working memory enhances gamma oscillations in rodent olfactory bulb and medial prefrontal cortex
papers.reason: The paper directly reports animal neural oscillation and connectivity findings during spatial working memory, including medial prefrontal gamma dynamics linked to behaviour.

papers.title: Neural correlates of ketamine-induced dilation of temporal expectation
papers.reason: The study links macaque timing behaviour to cortical ramping and population dynamics under ketamine, offering neural mechanisms relevant to modelling temporal expectation and decision processes.

papers.title: [Neurophysiological differentiation of children with ADHD alone and ADHD comorbid with dyslexia: a P600-like component analysis].
papers.reason: The title indicates an EEG/ERP-based differentiation of clinical child groups involving ADHD, but the apparent focus on a P600-like language component makes the executive-function relevance partial.
